text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: p99 streaming latency > 2.0s and p95 > 800ms for Route /v1/stream in eu-west-2. Alerts from perf-monitor. Affected shards: streaming-*-eu-west-2. Severity: P2. Paging oncall.

maya: Ack. I'm oncall, grabbing triage. Paging @liam (netops) and @sarah (sre).

liam: Looking. Any nginx upstream 502s? I see cloudmetrics spike on TLS handshake retries across AZs AZB->AZC.

sarah: Confirmed p99 tail stalls at 2.3s for streaming tail tokens, lots of retransmits. No 5xx surge though, just stalled frames.

maya: Customer impact: interactive streaming stalls for ~10-30s windows. Early reports from 12 tenants, mostly eu-west-2. No major request loss but UX broken.

liam: Running quick traceroute from egress-host-12 to client-facing-nat:
```
traceroute -n -w 1 -q 1 10.10.200.1
1 10.10.1.1 0.68 ms
2 10.10.2.5 1.12 ms
3 10.240.200.2 120.32 ms  <-- inter-AZ hop spike
```
Looks like cross-AZ path is spiking. Also seeing NAT ephemeral exhaustion on nat-gw-azc (see conntrack logs).

maya: Can we fail traffic to nat-gw-azb or drain azc? If we shift egress to AZB it might avoid the bad path.

liam: I'll update route policy for the streaming subnet to prefer AZB egress and toggle connection tracking on nat-gw-azc (recycle conntrack table). Doing it now, small disruption expected.

ops-luke: FYI I pushed a canary config: set streaming route preference=azb for 10% of shards to test. Monitoring CPU and handshake RTT.

sarah: Observability: p99 latency dropped from 2.3s -> 1.1s for the canary group, retransmits down 60%. Good sign.

liam: Proceeding to shift remaining shards to AZB egress. Also issuing a graceful restart of nat-gw-azc to clear ephemeral port saturation: `aws ec2 reboot-instances --instance-ids i-0azc1234`.

maya: Noting mitigation steps in incident timeline. Assigning follow-up: create action item to increase NAT ephemeral port range and enable advanced conntrack metrics.

backend-eli: Any need to fallback model variant to reduce token rate? We have some heavy streaming sessions, but network looks primary. No fallback for now.

liam: nat restart done. Post-restart metrics show TLS handshake RTT normalized across AZs. p95 now ~220ms, p99 ~560ms for streaming endpoints in eu-west-2.

maya: Marking triage: mitigated. Keeping incident open for postmortem and runbook updates. Owners: liam (network mitigation), sarah (observability), maya (postmortem).

sarah: Please capture packet captures from the affected window and save to s3://redwood-incident-captures/2350004321.pcap for root cause analysis.

maya: Thanks all. Final note: customers notified via status page about degraded streaming in eu-west-2; update when we close.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager duty escalation canceled.
